# Time for Some Introductions!

---

# Course Structure
- **Total Sessions:** 13
- **Course Structure:**
  - **Lecture:** 1HR 15MIN
  - **Break:** 15MIN
  - **Labs:** 1HR
- **Labs:** Weekly
- **Homeworks:** Bi-Weekly
- **Final Project?** Yes! And it will be a group project.
- **Final Exam?** Nope! Not a believer in exams.
- **Quizzes:** 4, lowest grade will be dropped. 
  
---

# Course Structure
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Data Gathering] --> B[Data Manipulation]
  B --> C[Exploratory Data Analysis]
  C --> D[Data Visualization]
  D --> E[Data Modeling]
  E --> F[Result Presentation]
```
- This course will follow the general procedure of how Data Science project is done
- By the end of the course, the goal is for you to be comfortable with completing a Data Scinece project on your own

---

# Labs
- Each lab will be a series of R coding exercises 
- We will try to complete most of it during the lab hour
- If not completed, your task will be to finish what is left, and submit the R Script
- The point of these labs are to give you a repository of codes that you can reuse for your future work. 
- So explore, and have fun!
- **Important Note:** At any given point in time during the lab session, feel free to stop me to ask any questions. If you haven't been able to, office hour will be there too!
  
---

# Homeworks
- Homeworks are submitted on a bi-weekly basis
- Each week, you will submit a "portion" of a Data Science Report
- At the end of all the homeworks, you will have a full Data Science Report
- Goal is to get you a template of a Data Science report to fall back on

---

# Final Project
- Final Project will be replication of the homeworks
- With the dataset of your choosing, you will leverage all the DS toolkits you have learned throughout the semester to do a Data Science project
- **Final Deliverables:** Data Science report and a presentation
- This will be a group project (pending enrollment)

---

# Some Ground Rules
- No such thing as "Dumb Question"
- After each lecture, please don't hesitate to give me feedback
- Let's try our best to put away our phones during lecture
- LLMs are your friend, use them! But.. understand what it's doing

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
```

---

# Environment Setup - R

:::{.columns}
:::{.column}
**Mac OS**  
- Go to the CRAN R download page.  
- Under macOS, download the latest `.pkg` installer   
- Open the `.pkg` installer and accept defaults.  
- It will install R under: `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework`. 
::: 

:::{.column}
**Windows (Windows 10/11)**  
  - Go to the R download page (CRAN).  
  - Download the latest R for Windows (`base`).   
  - Run the installer and accept all default options.  
:::
:::

---

# Environment Setup - R

:::{.columns}
:::{.column}
**Mac OS**  
- Go to the RStudio (Posit) download page.   
- Download RStudio Desktop (free) for macOS.   
- Open the .dmg and drag RStudio into Applications.   
:::

:::{.column}
**Windows (Windows 10/11)**  
- Go to the RStudio (Posit) download page.   
- Download RStudio Desktop (free) for Windows.   
- Run the installer and accept defaults.   
:::
:::

---


# Environment Setup - Quarto

:::{.columns}
:::{.column}
**Mac OS**  
- Go to the Quarto download page.   
- Download the macOS installer (.pkg) and run it.   
- Restart RStudio if it was open.   
:::

:::{.column}
**Windows (Windows 10/11)**   
- Go to the Quarto download page.   
- Download the Windows installer (.msi) and run it.   
- Restart RStudio if it was open.   
:::
:::

---

# Environment Setup - Testing
- Open RStudio.
- In the console, run:
```r
R.version.string
install.packages("quarto")      
quarto::quarto_version()
```
- Go to: File → New File → Quarto Document → choose HTML → Render.

- If a web preview opens, everything works 🎉
